reference.source: Firestein & Kelley's Textbook of Rheumatology / EULAR recommendations for autoinflammatory diseases
clinicalPearls: A spectrum of autosomal dominant disorders caused by gain-of-function mutations in NLRP3 (CIAS1), encoding cryopyrin
The spectrum spans mild familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome, intermediate Muckle-Wells syndrome, and severe neonatal-onset multisystem inflammatory disease (NOMID/CINCA)
A recurrent urticaria-like (neutrophilic) rash with fever, arthralgia and conjunctivitis is common across the spectrum
Cold exposure is a classic trigger in the milder familial cold form
Sensorineural hearing loss is a hallmark of Muckle-Wells syndrome, and chronic aseptic meningitis with developmental delay and bony overgrowth characterises NOMID
AA amyloidosis is a serious long-term complication of the more severe phenotypes
Disease is exquisitely responsive to interleukin-1 inhibition, which can prevent progression of organ damage if started early
reference.pathophysiology: Cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes are driven by gain-of-function mutations in NLRP3, which encodes cryopyrin, a sensor protein of the innate immune system. Cryopyrin nucleates the NLRP3 inflammasome, a multiprotein complex that activates caspase-1. The mutations lower the threshold for or constitutively enhance inflammasome assembly, leading to excessive caspase-1-mediated cleavage of pro-interleukin-1 beta into its active form. The resulting overproduction of interleukin-1 beta produces systemic and organ-specific inflammation, and the severity of the phenotype broadly tracks the degree of inflammasome dysregulation. Chronic interleukin-1-driven inflammation underlies the sensorineural deafness, central nervous system disease, and predisposition to AA amyloidosis.
additionalDifferentials: Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis or adult-onset Still disease
Other hereditary periodic fever syndromes (TRAPS, hyper-IgD syndrome, familial Mediterranean fever)
Chronic infective or aseptic meningitis (for NOMID)
Deficiency of the interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (DIRA)
additionalInvestigations: Acute phase reactants (C-reactive protein and serum amyloid A)
Genetic testing of NLRP3, including analysis for somatic mosaicism when routine testing is negative
Audiometry to detect sensorineural hearing loss
Ophthalmology assessment for conjunctivitis, uveitis and papilloedema
Cerebrospinal fluid examination and neuroimaging in suspected NOMID
Urinalysis for proteinuria to screen for AA amyloidosis
redFlags: New or progressive sensorineural hearing loss
Features of central nervous system involvement such as chronic headache, raised intracranial pressure or developmental regression in neonatal-onset disease
Visual compromise from papilloedema or uveitis
reference.prognosis: Milder cold-induced disease has a favourable outlook, but untreated Muckle-Wells syndrome and NOMID cause progressive deafness, neurological damage and amyloidosis; early and sustained interleukin-1 inhibition can halt organ damage and greatly improve prognosis.
pitfalls: Mislabelling the recurrent rash as ordinary allergic urticaria and giving antihistamines
Missing the diagnosis when standard NLRP3 sequencing is negative because of somatic mosaicism
Delaying interleukin-1 blockade until irreversible hearing or neurological damage has occurred
references: EULAR recommendations for the management of autoinflammatory diseases
management: Use interleukin-1 blockade with anakinra, canakinumab or rilonacept as the definitive therapy that suppresses the IL-1-driven inflammation of CAPS
Initiate sustained IL-1 inhibition early, particularly in Muckle-Wells syndrome and NOMID, to prevent progressive deafness, neurological injury and amyloidosis
Advise cold-trigger avoidance in the milder familial cold autoinflammatory form
Monitor acute-phase reactants (C-reactive protein and serum amyloid A) and perform serial audiometry to detect sensorineural hearing loss
Arrange ophthalmology review for conjunctivitis, uveitis and papilloedema, and manage chronic aseptic meningitis and raised intracranial pressure in NOMID
Screen for AA amyloidosis with urinalysis for proteinuria
Provide genetic counselling for this autosomal dominant NLRP3 disorder, with family testing and consideration of somatic mosaicism
